cards.front: How do roadside response vehicles mark an emergency zone?
cards.back: Emergency zones may use flares or signs, but roadside response vehicles mark them with flashing lights.

cards.front: What must you do when you see a roadside response vehicle with flashing lights?
cards.back: When you see a roadside response vehicle with flashing lights you must either move into a lane farther away or slow to at least ten miles per hour under the posted limit.

cards.front: What is the top speed allowed in an emergency zone?
cards.back: You must never go faster than fifty miles per hour in an emergency zone.

cards.front: Which vehicles count as roadside response vehicles?
cards.back: Roadside response vehicles include tow trucks, garbage trucks, incident response, highway maintenance and utility vehicles as well as police, fire trucks and ambulances.

cards.front: Near a roadside response vehicle, must you both move over and slow down?
cards.back: Near a roadside response vehicle with flashing lights, moving over and slowing to at least ten miles per hour under the limit are alternatives, and you must do one of them.

cards.front: How do the slow-down amount and the emergency zone ceiling differ?
cards.back: In an emergency zone, slowing to ten miles per hour under the posted limit is a minimum drop, and fifty miles per hour is an absolute ceiling no matter how high the posted limit is.

cards.front: Where are you responsible for parking, and what can colored curbs tell you?
cards.back: You are responsible for parking only in designated areas so your vehicle is not a hazard, and colored curbs can signal parking limits.

cards.front: Which places may you never park in?
cards.back: Never park in an intersection or on a crosswalk, a sidewalk or a bicycle lane.

cards.front: How far from a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign must you park?
cards.back: Do not park within thirty feet of a traffic signal, a stop sign or a yield sign.

cards.front: How far from a driveway, alley or private road must you park?
cards.back: Do not park within five feet of a driveway, an alley or a private road.

cards.front: How far from a fire station driveway across the street must you park?
cards.back: Do not park within seventy-five feet of a fire station driveway when parking on the opposite side of the street.

cards.front: Which no-parking gaps apply to signs, driveways and fire stations?
cards.back: The thirty-foot gap applies to traffic signals, stop signs and yield signs, the five-foot gap to driveways, alleys and private roads, and the seventy-five-foot gap to a fire station driveway across the street.

cards.front: How far from a pedestrian safety zone must you park?
cards.back: Do not park within twenty feet of a pedestrian safety zone.

cards.front: What are the parking rules near railroad tracks and crossings?
cards.back: Never park on railroad tracks or within fifty feet of a railroad crossing.

cards.front: How far from a fire hydrant must you park?
cards.back: Do not park within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant.

cards.front: Which no-parking gaps apply to hydrants, safety zones and railroad crossings?
cards.back: Fire hydrants need a fifteen-foot gap, pedestrian safety zones a twenty-foot gap and railroad crossings a fifty-foot gap, while the tracks themselves allow no parking at all.

cards.front: Which way must a parked car face, and how close to the curb?
cards.back: A parked vehicle must face the same way as traffic and sit no more than twelve inches from the curb.

cards.front: Where else is parking banned?
cards.back: Parking is banned beside an already parked vehicle, in a construction zone, on a bridge, overpass, tunnel or underpass, and on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

cards.front: What do white, yellow and red curbs mean?
cards.back: A white painted curb allows only short stops, while a yellow or red curb marks a loading zone or another restriction.
cards.memory_hook: white brief, yellow or red limits

cards.front: How do the curb-distance rule and the curb-color rules fit together?
cards.back: The twelve-inch limit is a maximum distance from the curb, and white curbs allow brief stops while yellow or red curbs mean loading or other limits.

cards.front: When should you set the parking brake?
cards.back: Set the parking brake every time you park, and especially on a hill.

cards.front: What is the Dutch Reach?
cards.back: The Dutch Reach means checking your mirrors, then opening the door with the hand farthest from it, which turns your body so you see approaching cyclists.

cards.front: What is the rule for a child under sixteen left in a running vehicle?
cards.back: Leaving a child younger than sixteen alone in a parked vehicle with the motor running is a crime.

cards.front: What is the rule for a child under twelve left alone in a parked vehicle?
cards.back: Leaving a child younger than twelve alone in a parked vehicle is a crime even with the motor off.

cards.front: How do the under-sixteen and under-twelve rules differ?
cards.back: The under-sixteen rule covers a child left in a parked vehicle with the engine running, while the under-twelve rule covers a child left alone in any parked vehicle.

cards.front: When is leaving an animal in a vehicle a crime?
cards.back: Leaving an animal alone in a vehicle is a crime when heat, cold, poor ventilation or lack of water could injure or kill it.

cards.front: What may police do if no one can open a vehicle with a child or animal inside?
cards.back: If nobody nearby can open the vehicle, police may remove a child or animal by any reasonable means, and the officer or agency is not liable for the damage.

cards.front: How do you pull into an angled or perpendicular space?
cards.back: To pull into a perpendicular or angled space, check traffic, signal, creep forward while steering to the middle of the space, center between the lines, then stop and secure the vehicle.

cards.front: How do you leave an angled or perpendicular space?
cards.back: To leave a perpendicular or angled space, back straight out while watching traffic until your bumper clears the next vehicle, then turn the wheel sharply the way you want to go.

cards.front: How do you start parallel parking?
cards.back: To parallel park, back slowly until your front bumper lines up with the rear bumper of the car you are parking behind, then turn the wheel sharply and back in.

cards.front: How do you finish parallel parking?
cards.back: Stop before you touch the bumper of the vehicle behind you, then pull forward so you end up no more than twelve inches from the curb.

cards.front: What marks the start and finish of parallel parking?
cards.back: Entering a parallel space starts by backing until bumpers line up with the car you park behind, and it ends no more than twelve inches from the curb.

cards.front: How do you leave a parallel parking space?
cards.back: When leaving a parallel space, signal, steer forward slowly, and move into the nearest lane once your front door passes the rear bumper of the car ahead.

cards.front: Facing uphill against a tall curb, which way do you turn the wheel?
cards.back: Facing uphill against a tall curb, turn the wheel away from the curb until the back of the front tire rests against it, so a rolling car stops at the curb.

cards.front: Facing uphill with a low or rounded curb, which way may be safer?
cards.back: Facing uphill with a low or rounded curb, turning the wheel toward the curb may be safer, because the car would then roll away from the road.

cards.front: How do tall and low uphill curbs differ for wheel position?
cards.back: Uphill against a tall curb you turn the wheel away so the tire's back edge catches the curb, but with a low or rounded uphill curb turning toward it may be safer.

cards.front: Facing downhill with a curb, which way do you turn the wheel?
cards.back: Facing downhill, turn the wheel toward the curb until the front of the front tire touches it.

cards.front: On a hill with no curb, which way do you turn the wheels?
cards.back: On a hill with no curb, turn the wheels toward the road edge so the car rolls away from traffic.

cards.front: How do downhill and no-curb wheel positions differ?
cards.back: Downhill the wheel turns toward the curb so the front of the tire meets it, and with no curb the wheels turn toward the road edge, away from traffic.

cards.front: What must stay clear beside a disabled parking space?
cards.back: The striped access aisle beside a disabled parking space must stay clear, and you can be fined for blocking it or parking there without the required placard.

cards.front: Who may apply for disabled parking, and how?
cards.back: A person whose disability limits or impairs walking may apply for temporary or permanent disabled parking by completing the application together with their physician.

cards.front: When may you park at an electric vehicle charging station?
cards.back: Parking at an electric vehicle charging station is illegal unless your vehicle is plugged into the charger.

cards.front: What rules apply when towing a boat, trailer or camper?
cards.back: When towing a boat, trailer or camper you must follow manufacturer, state and federal rules on weight, hookups, brakes and licensing.

cards.front: Is it legal to drive with an unsecured load?
cards.back: Driving with an unsecured load is illegal, so tie items down with rope, netting or straps and fasten large objects directly to the vehicle or trailer.

cards.front: When may an animal ride in a truck bed?
cards.back: Carrying an animal outside the cab, such as in a truck bed, is illegal unless it is in a protective harness or enclosure.

cards.front: What offense is transporting an animal in a dangerous way?
cards.back: Transporting an animal in a way that endangers it or the public is a misdemeanor under the state's animal cruelty laws.

cards.front: How do the truck-bed rule and the cruelty misdemeanor differ?
cards.back: An animal in a truck bed is legal only with a protective harness or enclosure, while transporting any animal in a risky way is a separate misdemeanor offense.

cards.front: Why is a loose pet in the car a problem?
cards.back: A loose pet or one on the driver's lap is a distraction, and any activity that pulls focus from safe driving is illegal.

cards.front: Do the rules of the road apply on Washington State Ferries?
cards.back: Washington State Ferries are part of the state highway network, so every rule of the road applies there.

cards.front: What are the rules about ferry lines?
cards.back: Cutting into a ferry line is a traffic offense that can bring a fine, and a holding lane must not block home driveways or intersections.

cards.front: Where is ocean beach driving allowed?
cards.back: Ocean beach driving is allowed only in Grays Harbor and Pacific counties, where the beach counts as a state highway.

cards.front: What is the beach speed limit, and who has the right-of-way?
cards.back: On the beach the speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour, and walkers and cyclists always have the right-of-way.

cards.front: What limits apply to beach driving?
cards.back: Beach driving is limited to two counties with a twenty-five miles per hour limit, and walkers and cyclists keep the right-of-way there at all times.

recap_hooks.text: Flashing lights mark emergency zones; move over or slow well below the limit, and never exceed the ceiling.
Tow trucks, garbage trucks and utility vehicles count, along with police, fire and ambulances.
Park only in designated areas, never in intersections, crosswalks, sidewalks or bike lanes.
Thirty feet from signs, five from driveways, seventy-five across from fire stations.
Twenty from safety zones, fifty from crossings, fifteen from hydrants, and never on tracks.
Face with traffic close to the curb, and read the curb color.
No double parking or parking on bridges or freeway shoulders; set the brake and use the Dutch Reach.
Never leave a child under sixteen with the engine running, or under twelve alone at all.
Leaving an animal in harmful conditions is a crime, and police may remove children or animals.
Creep into angled spaces and back straight out before turning.
Parallel park by lining up bumpers, backing in, stopping short and ending near the curb.
Uphill with a tall curb turn away; with a low curb toward may be safer.
Downhill turn toward the curb; with no curb, toward the road edge.
Keep disabled access aisles clear, apply with a physician, and park at chargers only while plugged in.
Follow towing rules, secure every load, and carry animals safely and never loose.
Ferries are state highways, so road rules apply and line cutting brings a fine.
Beach driving is allowed in two counties at a low limit, with walkers and cyclists first.
